title: Token-Budgeted Blackboard Coordination for Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a token-budgeted blackboard memory with selective publish/subscribe rules reduce communication overhead in multi-agent workflows without harming task success on decomposition-heavy AI tasks?
hypothesis: Replacing broad peer-to-peer message exchange with a shared blackboard that enforces token budgets and relevance-based publishing will lower latency and token cost while maintaining or improving end-task accuracy by reducing redundant coordination chatter.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around uncertainty-aware scheduling, adaptive replanning, and communication gating in multi-agent workflows, suggesting the space is active but crowded. A clear gap is a simpler systems-level intervention focused on coordination substrate design rather than yet another routing or gating heuristic. Because several communication-pruning and gating variants were already rejected, a blackboard-style coordination mechanism offers a distinct, testable alternative: instead of deciding whether agents should talk, it restructures how they share intermediate state under explicit token constraints. This directly targets a likely bottleneck in agentic workflow optimization—coordination overhead during task decomposition—while avoiding overlap with prior rejected proposals.
